findings.heading: Package errors / パッケージエラー
findings.proposition: The English names `plyr::summarise()` as a common source of masking errors; the Japanese names `plyr::summary()` instead, a function plyr does not export.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader hunting a masking conflict searches for `plyr::summary()`, finds no such function, and fails to recognise that the real conflict is between `plyr::summarise()` and `dplyr::summarise()`. Every other translation (fr, es, pt, ru, tr, vn) keeps `summarise()`, so this is a Japanese-only defect.

findings.heading: Plotting errors / プロットのエラー
findings.proposition: The English says the manual scale VALUES supplied (two colours) are insufficient for the number of factor levels; the Japanese says the NUMBER OF FACTOR LEVELS is insufficient (因子型の水準の数が十分ではありません), reversing which side of the mismatch is short.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader tries to add factor levels to the data, when the fix is to add a third colour to `scale_fill_manual(values = ...)`. The error text itself ("3 needed but only 2 provided") then reads as contradicting the surrounding explanation.

findings.heading: Plotting errors / プロットのエラー
findings.proposition: The English warns to consider whether NA has BECOME an extra factor level (a cause of the shortfall); the Japanese asks the reader to check whether NA is CORRECTLY a factor level (NA が正しく因子型の水準になっているか), presenting NA-as-a-level as the desired state rather than the suspected problem.
findings.reader_consequence: A Japanese reader treats an NA level as something to establish rather than as the unnoticed extra level that made two colours too few, so they do not remove or recount it and the plot still fails.

findings.heading: Common errors / よくあるエラー (chapter intro)
findings.proposition: The Japanese adds a translator's note stating that R error messages are not all translated into Japanese, and that where a Japanese version exists it is shown after the English one. The English has no such statement.
findings.reader_consequence: No harm to the reader: it correctly explains the paired English/Japanese code blocks that the translation adds throughout. Recorded because it is propositional content with no English counterpart, and because it governs how the rest of the chapter is read.
